resources.string: Officer needs accessibility settings to detect when the power menu is opened. Don’t worry—this is only used for security and has no malicious intent.
Officer uses this to put your screen to sleep if someone tries to power off your phone while it\'s locked.

On Android 13 and above, accessibility permission is blocked by default for applications that are not downloaded from the Google Play Store. However, you can still enable it by following these steps:

 1. Try to enable accessibility by clicking on the "Grant Accessibility Permission" button above.
 2. You will most probably see a "Restricted Setting" message. Make sure you open the popup dialog saying "For your security, this setting is currently unavailable".
 3. Only after this, go to the App info page of this app and click on the three dots menu in the top right corner.
 4. Click "Allow restricted settings".


Note: This is an open source application. Rest assured that this setting has no malicious intent.
Automatically turns the screen off for a set time if someone tries to power off your phone. Less convenient, but extra secure.

With this enabled, the screen turns off automatically if the power menu is opened. A timer starts, and the screen will keep putting itself to sleep until the timer ends. This makes it much harder for a thief to shut down your phone.

Different phones use different triggers for the power menu, so there\'s no one-size-fits-all solution. Open your power menu now, and the app will detect the events. Try the options below to see which one works for your device.
Automatically send an SMS if someone tries to power off from the lock screen. Optionally, attach the device location with it.

Different phone manufacturers have different event triggers which are broadcast when the power menu is opened. Hence, there is no one-size-fits-all solution. Once you give all the required permissions, use the custom trigger menu to complete the setup.
Set a custom trigger point for putting the screen to sleep. If the app is not working on your device, try setting this up.

Officer is an open source app, which helps in locating your phone in case of theft. No root or Shizuku required.

Usually, if you lose your phone, you can locate it using Google\'s \'Find My Device\' feature. However, that only works if your device is not switched off. Thieves take advantage of this, and they power off your phone to prevent tracking.

This app will prevent powering off your phone from the lock screen. It uses a workaround where, if anyone tries to open the power menu from the lock screen, it will put the display to sleep. But don\'t worry, if YOU want to power off your phone, you can unlock your screen and proceed as usual.
Enter the phone number and SIM to use for alerts. This is the number that will receive the SMS. Don\'t forget the country code!
Append the Google Maps location link to the SMS content.
Decide how many times you would like the app to ignore powering off attempts before sending the SMS. This is useful for preventing accidental alerts. The counting resets when you unlock your device.

Decide how many power-off attempts you would like the app to wait for after sending an SMS and before sending another one. Generally, once an SMS is sent, you have already been alerted, so there is technically no need for another one. Set the slider to \'-1\' if you don\'t want the alerts to be repeated in that session.
Broadcast an event when someone tries to power off from the lock screen. Useful for integrating with third party automation apps.

Broadcast an event when someone tries to power off from the lock screen. You can use automation routines with third party apps like Tasker and Macrodroid to trigger further actions on your phone. The intent will be named as \'com.akruzen.officer.ACTION_LOCK_TRIGGERED\'
Broadcast the event each and every time the power menu is triggered from the lock screen. Turning this OFF will broadcast the event only once per session.

I was returning home one evening in a rickshaw. When I got off to pay the driver, I realized I had left my phone on the seat. The driver immediately sped off, stealing my phone. I tried to track it using Google\'s \'Find My Device\', but unfortunately, he had switched it off. I hope my app helps people buy time to track their devices if this happens to them.
